title.fr: Le hockey, la crosse et le castor

text.en: More Canadians watch hockey than any other sport. It is seen as Canada's national winter sport.
text.fr: Les Canadiens regardent le hockey plus que tout autre sport. On le considère comme le sport national d'hiver du Canada.

source.quote: Hockey is Canada’s most popular spectator sport and is considered to be the national winter sport.

text.en: Ice hockey grew up in Canada in the 1800s.
text.fr: Le hockey sur glace s'est développé au Canada dans les années 1800.

source.quote: Ice hockey was developed in Canada in the 1800s.

text.en: Teams in the National Hockey League play to win the Stanley Cup. Lord Stanley, who was Governor General, gave the cup in 1892.
text.fr: Les équipes de la Ligue nationale de hockey jouent pour remporter la coupe Stanley. Lord Stanley, alors gouverneur général, a offert cette coupe en 1892.

source.quote: The National Hockey League plays for the championship Stanley Cup, donated by Lord Stanley, the Governor General, in 1892.

text.en: The Clarkson Cup is the prize in women's hockey. Adrienne Clarkson set it up in 2005. She was Canada's 26th Governor General and the first one of Asian origin.
text.fr: La coupe Clarkson est le trophée du hockey féminin. Adrienne Clarkson l'a créée en 2005. Elle a été la 26e gouverneure générale du Canada et la première d'origine asiatique.

source.quote: The Clarkson Cup, established in 2005 by Adrienne Clarkson, the 26th Governor General (and the first of Asian origin), is awarded for women’s hockey.

text.en: Canada's official summer sport is lacrosse. It is a very old game, and Aboriginal peoples were the first to play it.
text.fr: Le sport d'été officiel du Canada est la crosse. C'est un jeu très ancien, et ce sont les peuples autochtones qui y ont joué les premiers.

source.quote: Lacrosse, an ancient sport first played by Aboriginals, is the official summer sport.

text.en: Curling is a game played on ice. Scottish pioneers brought it here, and many Canadians enjoy it.
text.fr: Le curling est un jeu qui se pratique sur la glace. Des pionniers écossais l'ont apporté ici, et beaucoup de Canadiens l'apprécient.

source.quote: Curling, an ice game introduced by Scottish pioneers, is popular.

text.en: No game in Canada has more registered players than soccer.
text.fr: Aucun jeu au Canada ne compte plus de joueurs inscrits que le soccer.

source.quote: Soccer has the most registered players of any game in Canada.

text.en: Centuries ago, the Hudson's Bay Company chose the beaver as its symbol.
text.fr: Il y a des siècles, la Compagnie de la Baie d'Hudson a choisi le castor comme symbole.

source.quote: The beaver was adopted centuries ago as a symbol of the Hudson’s Bay Company.

text.en: In 1834, the St. Jean Baptiste Society, a patriotic group of French Canadians, took the beaver as one of its emblems. Other groups took it up as well.
text.fr: En 1834, la Société Saint-Jean-Baptiste, une association patriotique canadienne-française, a adopté le castor comme l'un de ses emblèmes. D'autres groupes l'ont aussi adopté.

source.quote: It became an emblem of the St. Jean Baptiste Society, a French-Canadian patriotic association, in 1834, and was also adopted by other groups.

text.en: You can find the hard-working beaver on the five-cent coin. Saskatchewan and Alberta have it on their coats of arms, and so do cities like Montreal and Toronto.
text.fr: On trouve le castor travailleur sur la pièce de cinq cents. La Saskatchewan et l'Alberta l'ont sur leurs armoiries, tout comme des villes telles que Montréal et Toronto.

source.quote: This industrious rodent can be seen on the five-cent coin, on the coats of arms of Saskatchewan and Alberta, and of cities such as Montreal and Toronto.
